title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends 105 Food Licences In Pre-Diwali Drive, Seizes Rs 1.35 Crore Stock
excerpt: In a separate two-day drive on November 4 and 5, the regulator suspended licences including Mumbai outlets linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Biryani By Kilo, shut seven establishments, and seized 39,485 kg of food articles ahead of Diwali.
body:
• Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended 105 food business licences and ordered seven establishments to shut in a special Diwali inspection drive on November 4 and 5, according to the FDA's statement reported by PTI.
  • Inspectors seized 39,485.42 kg of food articles worth Rs 1.35 crore from more than 70 establishments, including mawa, paneer, ghee, edible oils, farsan, dry fruits and sweets.
  • In Mumbai, the suspended licences included Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd (Blinkit) and Zepto Ltd, and reporting on the drive named Biryani By Kilo, Tossin Pizza in Worli and Jumbo Burger among the eateries facing the same action; a D-Mart outlet in Nagpur also faced action.
  • Consumers can report food-quality concerns to the FDA on its toll-free number, 1800222365, or through its Food and Drug Grievance Portal.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 105 food business outlets and ordered seven establishments to shut operations, in a special inspection drive carried out across the state on November 4 and 5 ahead of Diwali, the regulator said in a statement reported by PTI. The drive is a distinct, later action from the longer festive enforcement round the FDA summarised earlier in the week: this statement covers only the two days of November 4 and 5, and the establishments it names were not part of that earlier tally.

Who was suspended, and where

The 105 suspended licences were spread across the state: 39 in the Nashik division, 28 in Mumbai, 20 in Pune, 15 in Amravati, two in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and one in Thane, according to the FDA statement. In Mumbai, the list included Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd and Zepto Ltd, alongside food manufacturers, sweet shops, hotels, restaurants and caterers. Reporting on the drive by Dainik News Live named the Mumbai suspensions more specifically: Zepto in Worli and Blinkit (Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd), and eateries including Biryani By Kilo, Tossin Pizza in Worli and Jumbo Burger. The same report said a D-Mart outlet on Kamthi Road in Nagpur faced action, with refined soybean oil seized for breaching licence conditions. Licences were suspended over violations of food safety requirements, and the establishments concerned cannot conduct food business operations during the suspension period, the FDA stated.

What inspectors said they found

The inspections found violations including unhygienic manufacturing and storage conditions, improper food handling and packaging, lack of pest control, absence of temperature-control arrangements and non-availability of mandatory records and certificates, according to the statement reported by PTI. A fuller account of the FDA statement, reported by Urban Acres, added damaged or blackened walls and ceilings, food stored directly on floors, inadequate packaging, missing protective window mesh, and missing food-safety management plans, drinking-water analysis reports, medical-fitness certificates for food handlers and food safety training records at some premises. The inspections focused on products in high festive demand — sweets, mawa or khoya, milk, paneer, ghee, edible oil, farsan, dry fruits, food colours, chocolates, bakery products, packaged food and gift hampers — and covered manufacturers, retailers, storage facilities, e-commerce platforms and quick-commerce dark stores as well as hotels, caterers and street-food outlets.

The seizures, in numbers

The FDA seized 39,485.42 kg of food articles worth Rs 1.35 crore — Rs 1,35,70,098 in the department's figure — from more than 70 establishments during the two-day drive. The Pune division accounted for the highest seizure, food articles worth Rs 49.36 lakh weighing 14,429.7 kg, followed by the Konkan division at Rs 32.52 lakh and Nashik at Rs 28.35 lakh; in Mumbai, 2,396 kg of food products valued at Rs 13.87 lakh was seized. Separately, the administration seized prohibited food products, including gutkha and pan masala, worth Rs 7.96 lakh from three locations; three FIRs were registered, two persons were arrested, two vehicles worth Rs 4.70 lakh were seized and two establishments were sealed in connection with those seizures, PTI reported.

The seven establishments ordered shut

Of the seven closure orders, three were in Pune, two in Amravati and one each in the Mumbai and Konkan divisions. In Mumbai, Rajdhani Biryani Centre in Borivali West was ordered shut; the FDA said it had violated Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses Regulations, 2011. Aaradhana Dryfruit Sweets in Bhiwandi, in Thane district, was found manufacturing without a valid licence, and officials seized 1,780 kg of cashew, kaju katli, kunda and sweet barfi from the premises. In Pune, Shree Ganesh Ladduwale in Shikrapur, Pournima Sweets in Wanwadi and Sirvi Sweets in Bibwewadi were ordered to close over suspected substandard or unsafe food and hygiene violations, and in Amravati's division, Jay Gajanan Farsan in Washim was found operating without the required registration and Laxmi Bikaner in Amravati without a licence and in unhygienic conditions.

FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said ensuring access to safe and quality food during Diwali was the department's priority, and that businesses of all sizes and brands would face action for violating food-safety regulations, while stating that the purpose of enforcement was to promote compliance rather than harass businesses, according to the Urban Acres report. For shoppers buying sweets, dairy and packaged food in Maharashtra this Diwali, the sourced next step is the regulator's own channel: food-quality concerns can be reported on the FDA's toll-free number, 1800222365, or through its Food and Drug Grievance Portal.
